fix: Compare against the borrowed state without cloning and clone only when changed: let state = self.state.borrow(); let changed = self.active.len() != state.active.len() || self.active.iter().zip(&state.active).any(|(l, r)| l.id != r.id || l.depth != r.depth); if changed { ...; self.active.clear(); self.active.extend_from_slice(&state.active); ... }. This removes a Vec allocation on every layout pass.

fix: Add a field positions: Vec<usize> to TreeRenderSliver. In perform_layout: let mut positions = std::mem::take(&mut self.positions); positions.clear(); positions.extend(range); ...; then restore it with self.positions = positions before returning. The buffer is reused across frames, so the steady state does not allocate.

While any animation runs, perform_layout allocates a snapshot Vec (animation_snapshots, plus a direct_child_ids Vec per animation at line 278) and a HashSet (lines 800-803) every frame. Keep the snapshot Vec and the id set as reused fields and clear them each frame. Replace the HashSet with a retain over animation_distances that checks animations.iter().any(|a| a.parent_id == *id), which is cheap for the few animations in flight. Store direct_child_ids as a reused buffer or as a range into a shared Vec.

The RefCell borrow from line 839 stays alive while the app-supplied row builder runs (line 863). A builder that calls a TreeSliverController mutator (toggle_node, expand_all and so on) hits with_state_mut's borrow_mut and panics with BorrowMutError. Make with_state_mut use try_borrow_mut and return None on conflict, and document in the TreeSliver builder docs that the builder must not mutate the controller. Alternatively, drop the borrow before calling the builder by collecting the rows' node references in a second pass, which needs a clone and is the costlier option.

Scan once: let position = self.active.iter().position(|row| row.id == *id)?; Some(self.extent_at(position, &self.active[position])). The same node is currently searched twice per direct child, and this runs once per animating parent.

animation_shift (called once per visible row at line 849) and row_animation (line 753) each rescan self.active and the animations list. That makes each frame O(visible rows x animations x active rows). Resolve each snapshot's parent position once per layout, store it as parent_position: Option<usize> on TreeAnimationSnapshot (or in a reused buffer), and have animation_shift and row_animation read that field.

fix: find_node is a recursive whole-tree search, so each visible row costs O(total nodes) per frame. Record each active row's child-index path in flatten_nodes into a flat reused buffer, then resolve nodes by walking that path, so lookup is O(depth). extent_at (line 730) has the same cost for unmeasured rows and should use the same lookup.
